teaser.text: China Resources Land Limited builds property to sell, keeps property to rent, and manages space for fees. To understand how a dollar comes in and goes out, follow each business from the customer’s payment to the cost and obligation left behind.

stock.title: China Resources Land stock forecast
stock.meta_description: China Resources Land's forecast weighs development profit, recurring rental income, cash conversion and debt.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario is HKD13.25 in October 2027 and HKD25.21 by October 2029. It hinges on whether development profit recovers while rental and asset-light results support the business.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how China Resources Land operates, compares with rivals, assesses management, and weighs its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could China Resources Land's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s central message is that the shares fall sharply first and recover only partway by October 2029. The weighted price is HKD13.25 in October 2027, a 53% loss including dividends. It reaches HKD19.17 in October 2028, a 30% loss. By October 2029, it reaches HKD25.21, still a 6% loss from today’s HKD31.06.

blocks.heading: What must go right or wrong for China Resources Land?

paragraphs.text: Profit is the main swing factor. The base case uses normal operating profit of RMB41bn in the first period. It rises to RMB46bn and RMB49bn thereafter. The path begins below the historical cycle average of about RMB49.2bn because first-half 2026 segment results fell 32.5% year on year. Rental and asset-light results provide support, but development remains the largest exposure.

The bear case uses RMB30bn initially. It reaches RMB34bn and then RMB38bn, assuming weak development results persist. The bull case uses RMB48bn first. It rises to RMB55bn and RMB60bn, requiring stronger core-city sales, margin recovery and successful mall expansion. Management’s mall and housing targets support capacity, not profit guidance.

blocks.heading: How much cash does China Resources Land really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow rose from RMB19,382.466 million in 2024 to RMB22,724.039 million in 2025 even though operating cash flow fell. Capital spending fell to RMB6,787.676 million. The company therefore spent less, rather than clearly earning more from each project. Land and construction payments already included in operating cash flow should not be deducted again.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for China Resources Land?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash left after selected investment spending, not cash automatically available for dividends. Buying less land can strengthen cash today while shrinking tomorrow’s development pipeline. At year-end 2025, borrowings were RMB281.47 billion against RMB116.99 billion of cash. The 37% payout from core profit provides room, but debt service and construction commitments come first.

dividend.title: China Resources Land dividend
dividend.meta_description: China Resources Land dividend coverage, history, plans and yield in plain English.
dividend.opening: China Resources Land proposed a final 2025 dividend of RMB0.966 per share, down from RMB1.119. In 2025, free cash flow reached RMB22,724.039 million and, after dividends and minority distributions, RMB9,729.79 million remained.
dividend.closing: The full memo also covers China Resources Land’s business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does China Resources Land pay per share?

paragraphs.text: CR Land also proposed a final 2025 dividend of RMB0.966 per share, down from RMB1.119. Together, the share sale, proposed property trust and lower dividend release capital, but each gives something up: future ownership, future rent or immediate shareholder income.

blocks.heading: Is China Resources Land’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The position improved from 2023. Free cash flow reached RMB22,724.039 million in 2025, compared with RMB19,382.466 million in 2024. After 2025 dividends, RMB9,389.662 million, and minority distributions, RMB3,604.587 million, RMB9,729.79 million remained.

blocks.heading: What could change China Resources Land’s dividend?

paragraphs.text: Dividends reflect weaker recent earnings. The base case uses RMB1.15 per share first. It rises to RMB1.20 and RMB1.25 as recurring profit grows. The bear case cuts DPS to RMB1.05, then RMB0.95 and RMB0.90, consistent with the proposed reduction in the 2025 final dividend and negative first-half 2026 free cash flow. The bull case reaches RMB1.25, RMB1.40 and RMB1.55, requiring stronger cash conversion and asset recycling.

The bull path requires stronger tenant sales, occupancy and effective rents through 2027–28. By October 2029, the decisive evidence would be asset exits that release more cash than retained-income losses, allowing debt reduction and a higher earnings multiple.
